FINAL IVX ENTERPRISE AUTHENTICATION RECOVERY
FIX OWNER LOGIN AND BUILD RELIABLE PASSWORD AUTH FOR EVERY USER

EXECUTE NOW — DO NOT BYPASS SUPABASE AUTH
DO NOT HARDCODE A PASSWORD
DO NOT PRINT OR LOG PASSWORDS
DO NOT CLAIM FIXED UNTIL PHYSICAL-DEVICE LOGIN, RECOVERY, SESSION, AND ROLE TESTS PASS

==================================================
CRITICAL SECURITY INCIDENT
==================================================

An owner password was visible in a screenshot.

Treat that password as compromised.

Immediately:

1. Stop displaying password values in screenshots, logs, analytics, alerts, and proof reports.
2. Redact all password fields as ********.
3. Search logs and stored debugging artifacts for the exposed password.
4. Delete or sanitize any stored artifact containing it.
5. Reset the owner password through the approved recovery flow.
6. Revoke existing owner sessions after the new password is established.
7. Do not reuse the exposed password in IVX or any other service.
8. Record the incident without recording the password value.

==================================================
CURRENT VERIFIED ERROR
==================================================

Email checked:
iperez4242@gmail.com

Supabase response:

message: Invalid login credentials
code: invalid_credentials
HTTP status: 400
type: AuthApiError

This means Supabase rejected the submitted email/password pair.

Do not treat this as:

- owner-role failure;
- RLS failure;
- Admin Hub failure;
- mobile navigation failure;
- missing owner approval;
- generic backend outage.

Authentication must succeed before owner authorization is evaluated.

==================================================
PHASE 1 — FREEZE REPEATED LOGIN ATTEMPTS
==================================================

Do not continue submitting the same password.

1. Stop automated login retries.
2. Stop retry loops on HTTP 400 invalid_credentials.
3. Do not retry invalid credentials in the background.
4. Keep rate limiting, but do not use a device-only custom lock as the primary security system.
5. Display one clear error and recovery action.
6. Never disclose whether another person’s email exists.
7. For the configured owner account, show a secure “Reset owner password” action.

The client must not transform passwords except preserving the exact intended value.

Do not:

- lowercase passwords;
- normalize password characters;
- remove internal spaces;
- replace symbols;
- convert Unicode;
- truncate characters.

Only remove accidental leading/trailing whitespace if the UX explicitly warns the user before submission. Prefer sending the exact entered password.

==================================================
PHASE 2 — VERIFY THE ACTIVE SUPABASE PROJECT
==================================================

Before changing the user, prove the application is connected to the correct production Supabase project.

Return without exposing secret values:

- production project reference;
- production Supabase URL hostname;
- environment name;
- APK build version;
- backend runtime environment;
- auth client source file;
- variable names used;
- whether mobile and backend reference the same project;
- current auth provider configuration;
- evidence that no staging/development URL is loaded.

Compare:

ANDROID APK SUPABASE PROJECT
WEB SUPABASE PROJECT
BACKEND SUPABASE PROJECT
EXPECTED PRODUCTION PROJECT

Required result:

ALL PROJECT REFERENCES MATCH: TRUE

If false:

- correct environment binding;
- rebuild the affected client;
- do not reset the user in the wrong project.

==================================================
PHASE 3 — AUDIT THE OWNER AUTH USER
==================================================

Using the Supabase Admin API or dashboard under owner-controlled credentials, inspect the owner account without exposing secrets.

Verify:

- user exists;
- exact normalized email;
- email identity is attached;
- email confirmed status;
- user ID;
- banned status;
- deletion status;
- account creation timestamp;
- last sign-in timestamp;
- identities count;
- MFA enrollment state;
- app metadata;
- user metadata.

Do not retrieve or attempt to read a password. Password hashes are not application-readable.

Required output:

OWNER USER EXISTS: YES / NO
EMAIL MATCH: YES / NO
EMAIL CONFIRMED: YES / NO
ACCOUNT BANNED: YES / NO
IDENTITY VALID: YES / NO
PRODUCTION PROJECT MATCH: YES / NO

If the user does not exist, do not silently create a duplicate account. Report the exact finding and recover the canonical owner identity safely.

==================================================
PHASE 4 — RESET THE OWNER PASSWORD CORRECTLY
==================================================

Implement and verify the official password-recovery flow.

Required flow:

1. Owner taps “Forgot password.”
2. App calls the Supabase password-reset method for the owner email.
3. Supabase sends the recovery email through the configured production SMTP.
4. Recovery link opens the correct IVX deep link or web recovery route.
5. Recovery code/session is exchanged securely.
6. Owner enters a new password twice.
7. Password-strength requirements are validated.
8. Password is updated through the authenticated recovery session.
9. All previous owner sessions are revoked.
10. Owner signs in manually using the new password.
11. Session is persisted securely.
12. Owner role is verified server-side.
13. Owner Dashboard and Admin Hub open.

Do not place passwords in:

- URL parameters;
- logs;
- analytics;
- screenshots;
- local plaintext storage;
- chat messages;
- proof ledgers.

==================================================
PHASE 5 — PASSWORD POLICY FOR ALL USERS
==================================================

Apply one enterprise policy to owners, admins, members, investors, buyers, realtors, and staff.

Recommended policy:

- minimum 12 characters;
- allow long passphrases;
- maximum length at least 64 characters;
- accept password-manager-generated passwords;
- support symbols and spaces;
- reject known leaked passwords when the provider supports it;
- do not require arbitrary frequent password changes;
- require reauthentication before sensitive password/security changes;
- never email plaintext passwords;
- never let administrators view user passwords.

Owner and privileged accounts:

- require MFA;
- require recent authentication for dangerous operations;
- notify owner of new-device sign-in;
- allow session review and revocation;
- add recovery codes if supported.

Do not apply MFA to every ordinary user without first testing recovery and support workflows.

==================================================
PHASE 6 — FIX THE LOGIN CLIENT
==================================================

Audit every login implementation on Android, iOS, and web.

Use one canonical authentication service.

Required login behavior:

1. Normalize email with trim + lowercase.
2. Preserve password contents exactly.
3. Submit once.
4. Disable the button while submitting.
5. Attach a unique trace ID.
6. Apply a reasonable request timeout.
7. Handle exact Supabase error codes.
8. Never automatically retry invalid_credentials.
9. Clear the password field after repeated failure or when leaving the screen.
10. Do not expose detailed internal Auth errors to ordinary users.
11. Permit diagnostic detail only in an owner-only diagnostics drawer.
12. Store the session securely, never the password.

User-facing error:

“Email or password is incorrect. Try again or reset your password.”

Owner diagnostics may show:

- error code;
- HTTP status;
- trace ID;
- project reference;
- timestamp.

Never show:

- submitted password;
- auth keys;
- raw access token;
- raw refresh token.

==================================================
PHASE 7 — REMOVE CUSTOM AUTHENTICATION CONFLICTS
==================================================

Search for conflicting logic:

- hardcoded owner passwords;
- local password comparison;
- fallback passwords;
- automatic owner session injection;
- bypass-owner-login flags;
- duplicate Supabase clients;
- stale environment variables;
- staging auth URLs;
- manual JWT creation;
- cached invalid sessions;
- old AsyncStorage session keys;
- custom cooldown counters;
- multiple login endpoints;
- backend and frontend both attempting password sign-in independently.

There must be one authoritative password authenticator:

SUPABASE AUTH

IVX authorization occurs only after successful authentication.

==================================================
PHASE 8 — SESSION MANAGEMENT
==================================================

Implement reliable enterprise session handling:

- short-lived access token;
- refresh-token rotation through the Supabase client;
- secure local session storage;
- auto-refresh while active;
- refresh after app foreground;
- clean sign-out;
- session revocation;
- session expiry handling;
- password-change session invalidation;
- account-disabled handling;
- no infinite refresh loops.

On app launch:

1. Load the saved session.
2. Validate/refresh it.
3. Call the server to verify user and role.
4. Open the authorized route.
5. If refresh fails, clear the invalid session and show login.
6. Never fall back to a fake owner session.

==================================================
PHASE 9 — AUTHENTICATION VS AUTHORIZATION
==================================================

Keep these separate:

AUTHENTICATION:
Is this email/password/session valid?

AUTHORIZATION:
May this authenticated user access this feature?

After Supabase authentication succeeds:

1. Fetch the canonical profile by auth user ID.
2. Determine roles server-side.
3. Verify owner status using immutable owner configuration or database role.
4. Enforce owner-only routes on the backend.
5. Apply RLS to user-owned data.
6. Do not rely on a hidden mobile screen or email comparison alone.

Test roles:

- owner;
- admin;
- member;
- investor;
- buyer;
- realtor;
- unauthenticated user;
- suspended user.

==================================================
PHASE 10 — RATE LIMITING AND ABUSE PROTECTION
==================================================

Use provider/server rate limits plus controlled client UX.

Required:

- no unlimited password attempts;
- no automatic retries on invalid credentials;
- IP-aware rate limiting where architecture requires it;
- account and device abuse monitoring;
- escalating delays for repeated failures;
- CAPTCHA or additional challenge when abuse is detected;
- alerting for owner-account attacks;
- password reset rate limits;
- generic errors that prevent account enumeration.

Do not permanently lock the legitimate owner out solely because one phone recorded failed attempts.

Provide a secure recovery path.

==================================================
PHASE 11 — OWNER MFA
==================================================

After password recovery is proven:

1. Enroll the owner in TOTP authenticator MFA.
2. Verify challenge and recovery.
3. Require MFA for:
   - production deployment approval;
   - credential changes;
   - production-data deletion;
   - payment configuration;
   - DNS changes;
   - user-role elevation;
   - disabling MFA.
4. Test lost-device recovery.
5. Do not enable MFA until the recovery mechanism has been verified.

==================================================
PHASE 12 — EMAIL DELIVERY RELIABILITY
==================================================

Verify password recovery email end to end:

- production SMTP configured;
- sender domain authenticated;
- SPF;
- DKIM;
- DMARC;
- reset URL allowlist;
- Android deep link;
- iOS universal link;
- web callback;
- link expiry;
- one-time use;
- resend behavior;
- spam-folder guidance;
- delivery logging without sensitive contents.

Disable email-provider link tracking if it breaks or rewrites Supabase recovery links.

==================================================
PHASE 13 — MEMBER SELF-SERVICE
==================================================

Every member must have:

- Forgot password;
- secure reset email;
- change password while signed in;
- reauthentication before sensitive change;
- session logout from all devices;
- optional MFA;
- clear recovery status;
- support escalation without administrators seeing passwords.

Admin tools may:

- send recovery/invite links;
- disable an account;
- revoke sessions;
- view non-sensitive auth status.

Admin tools must never:

- display passwords;
- set a visible shared password;
- email plaintext passwords;
- impersonate a user without an audited support flow.

==================================================
PHASE 14 — DATABASE AND RLS QA
==================================================

Verify authentication-related data integrity:

- one profile per auth user;
- no duplicate owner profiles;
- profile auth_user_id is unique;
- deleted auth users handled safely;
- role values validated;
- owner role cannot be assigned by client input;
- RLS blocks cross-user reads and writes;
- service-role key never included in the mobile app;
- anon/publishable key is configured only as intended;
- backend verifies JWT claims.

==================================================
PHASE 15 — REQUIRED AUTOMATED TESTS
==================================================

Run tests for:

1. Correct owner password.
2. Incorrect owner password.
3. Owner password reset.
4. Expired recovery link.
5. Reused recovery link.
6. Email case normalization.
7. Password symbols preserved.
8. Password internal spaces preserved.
9. Leading/trailing password behavior is explicit.
10. Disabled account.
11. Unconfirmed email.
12. Expired access token.
13. Valid refresh token.
14. Invalid refresh token.
15. Logout.
16. Logout all devices.
17. App restart session restore.
18. Password change revokes old sessions.
19. Owner MFA success.
20. Owner MFA failure.
21. Member login.
22. Investor login.
23. Buyer login.
24. Unauthorized owner-route access.
25. Rate-limit response.
26. Offline login behavior.
27. Network timeout.
28. Wrong Supabase environment.
29. No password in logs.
30. No password in AsyncStorage.
31. No service-role key in mobile bundle.
32. Android login.
33. iOS login.
34. Web login.
35. Parallel login attempts.
36. Recovery email deep-link routing.
37. Account enumeration protection.
38. User session revocation.
39. Owner role server verification.
40. RLS role enforcement.

==================================================
PHASE 16 — PHYSICAL-DEVICE QA
==================================================

On Android:

1. Install the current production APK.
2. Clear old app data.
3. Open login.
4. Request password reset.
5. Open reset email.
6. Set the new password.
7. Sign in manually.
8. Open Owner Dashboard.
9. Open Admin Hub.
10. Restart app.
11. Confirm session restoration.
12. Logout.
13. Sign in again.
14. Enter a wrong password once.
15. Confirm recovery remains available.
16. Test network interruption.
17. Test background/foreground.
18. Confirm no crash.
19. Confirm password never appears in logs or UI after submission.
20. Capture timestamps, trace IDs, and screenshots with passwords redacted.

Repeat equivalent testing on web and iOS when available.

==================================================
PHASE 17 — REQUIRED PRODUCTION PROOF
==================================================

Return:

AUTH PROJECT:
Project reference:
Environment:
Mobile/backend project match:

OWNER USER:
Exists:
Email confirmed:
Banned:
Identity valid:
User ID redacted:

PASSWORD RECOVERY:
Reset request:
Email delivery:
Deep link:
Password update:
Old sessions revoked:
Manual sign-in:

SESSION:
Access refresh:
Restart persistence:

Logout all devices:

AUTHORIZATION:
Owner role:
Owner Dashboard:
Admin Hub:
Non-owner rejection:

SECURITY:
MFA:
Rate limiting:
Password redaction:
Service-role mobile exposure:
RLS:

TESTS:
Commands:
Passed:
Failed:
Skipped:
Typecheck:

DEPLOYMENT:
Repository:
Commit SHA:

Runtime SHA:
Health:

ANDROID:
APK:
Version:
Version code:
Source commit:
Physical-device result:

FINAL STATUS:
ENTERPRISE AUTHENTICATION VERIFIED
or
NOT VERIFIED — EXACT REMAINING BLOCKER

==================================================
MANDATORY ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
==================================================

Do not mark complete until:

[ ] The exposed owner password has been replaced.
[ ] The production Supabase project is confirmed.
[ ] The canonical owner Auth user is confirmed.
[ ] Password reset works end to end.
[ ] Manual owner login succeeds.
[ ] Old sessions are revoked.
[ ] Session survives restart.
[ ] Logout/login succeeds.
[ ] Non-owner access is rejected.
[ ] Passwords never appear in logs, screenshots, storage, or evidence.
[ ] Every user role has a recovery flow.
[ ] Rate limiting does not permanently lock out legitimate users.
[ ] Owner MFA and recovery are tested.
[ ] Android, web, and available iOS tests pass.
[ ] Production evidence is returned.

Do not “fix” this by bypassing Supabase, hardcoding the owner password, disabling password validation, creating a fake session, or automatically signing in the owner.

The required enterprise result is:

SECURE LOGIN
RELIABLE RECOVERY
DURABLE SESSION
SERVER-SIDE AUTHORIZATION
OWNER MFA
NO PASSWORD EXPOSURE,==================================================
PHASE 11 — OPTIONAL MFA IN SETTINGS
==================================================

Do not automatically activate MFA for the owner or for members.

MFA must be available as an optional security feature inside:

Settings
→ Security
→ Two-Factor Authentication

Default state:

MFA: OFF

The owner or user may choose to enable it.

Supported option:

- TOTP authenticator app

When MFA is OFF:

- normal email/password login continues;
- password recovery remains available;
- owner login must not be blocked;
- no MFA challenge is shown;
- dangerous operations remain protected by owner approval phrases.

When MFA is ON:

1. User opens Settings → Security.
2. User selects Enable Two-Factor Authentication.
3. App displays the authenticator QR code and manual setup key.
4. User enters the verification code.
5. Server verifies enrollment.
6. App shows MFA Enabled.
7. Recovery codes are generated if supported.
8. User may review and revoke trusted sessions.

Disabling MFA requires:

- current password or recent authentication;
- valid MFA code when currently enabled;
- confirmation;
- audit log entry.

MFA must never be activated silently.

MFA must never be required during the current owner-login recovery unless the owner already enabled it previously.

If an existing MFA enrollment is found:

- display the real enrollment status;
- allow the owner to complete the challenge;
- provide a secure recovery path;
- do not create a second duplicate enrollment.

==================================================
OPTIONAL MFA QA
==================================================

Test:

1. Owner login with MFA OFF.
2. Member login with MFA OFF.
3. Enable MFA from Settings.
4. Verify QR enrollment.
5. Verify correct TOTP code.
6. Reject incorrect TOTP code.
7. App restart with MFA enabled.
8. Disable MFA from Settings.
9. Password recovery while MFA is OFF.
10. Password recovery for an account with MFA enabled.
11. Confirm no user is automatically enrolled.
12. Confirm no owner is locked out because MFA is unavailable.

Required result:

DEFAULT MFA STATE: OFF
OWNER CAN ENABLE: PASS
OWNER CAN DISABLE: PASS
MEMBER CAN ENABLE: PASS
NORMAL LOGIN WITHOUT MFA: PASS
PASSWORD RECOVERY WITHOUT MFA: PASS
